title: Idle days in Hollywood
summary: He played ball in the park, learned that nobody goes to the office, and mistook downtown Los Angeles for Hollywood.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: The way you handle it you don't look as if you're drinking at all; you don't sound like you're drinking.
It all goes right to the ulcer.
And it sits there.
It just sits there and festers.
Oh, boy, that's awful. Do you have an ulcer?
Oh, yeah.
How can you drink?
What were we doing? Oh, we were in Hollywood.
We were in Hollywood, discussing the slow pace which I couldn't take.
What did you do with your time there? You obviously weren't writing all day.
When I didn't write, I was off playing ball in the park nearby.
You went to the office everyday?

At Paramount? Yes. Until we were told by the other people there that nobody goes to the office everyday in Hollywood. You go to the golf course; that's all I would hear is the golf course, we'll meet you at the golf course to discuss business.
Did you, in the classic way, buy yourself a long roadster?
No. I didn't have a car for quite a while out there. I took cars, we walked.
While I was at Paramount there wasn't too much going on; it got to be boring, very boring and I was living downtown in Los Angeles proper, thinking I was in Hollywood. I

wondered why the fabulous Hollywood that I always heard about looked so damn grimy and stinky, and it was ugly, and it had to be explained to me that this was not Hollywood, this was Los Angeles downtown. If I wanted to see what I'd always heard about I'd have to go thataway. So I went thataway and I discovered that there was indeed the pretty section of town, and then I moved up into Hollywood. That's terrific.
Confuse the transcriber.
So at some point you ran out of Hollywood, or Hollywood ran out of you.
Right.
